The danger in telling people life has no meaning

This is why nihilism, in my opinion, isn't a worthwhile philosophical position.

That's not to say it isn't valid. In fact, I'd say that it's so "valid" that it's ultimately trite. And that's part of the problem right there.

More to the point though, it misrepresents the nature of "meaning."

To say that life has no objective meaning is akin to saying that life has no objective flavor. Of course it has no objective meaning. But it's absolutely stuffed to the brim with subjective meaning.

To claim nihilism as a position is to fetishize the lack of objective meaning and ignore the reality and significance of subjective meaning. It's a fundamental error of reasoning, and a relatively destructive one. As you note, "Their life is still going to be guided subconsciously by a primary prerogative…only now they’re not going to be conscious or in control of it."

And since I was just hitting the high points there, that jumped around a fair bit. I presume you're aware enough of such issues that you can fill in the gaps.

On another note, this isn't the first response I've written to one of your posts - it's just the first one I've posted. The others (and yes - more than one) have similarly jumped around and hit a lot of points. You obviously have some understanding of such things, so I don't want to waste my time and yours with background and exposition, but it's sort of unsatisfying to just write a string of little snippets of thought, so I've thrown a few together, but never been satisfied enough with them to post them. But I have to post something sooner or later - clarity is a rare trait, and I don't like to let people who possess it slip away.
I'd love to hear all your thoughts, whether they jump around or not.
